rows.text: Upgrade/migration rollback protects settings, credentials and pending work.
rows.evidence: PARTIAL 2026-09-13. The data side is guarded and tested: the metadata store and the upload journal each carry a schema version, migrate forward inside one transaction that publishes the steps and the version together, and refuse a database newer than the build -- so an older package installed over a newer state stops with 'unsupported database schema version' rather than reading what it does not understand; migrations six, seven, eight and thirteen each keep pending work and are held to it; and a migration under a running daemon is refused (accounts::refuse_to_migrate_under_a_running_daemon, fail-closed on an unreadable file). Credentials live in the keyring under ids the settings file names and are touched by no migration. PACKAGE-LEVEL UPGRADE DONE 2026-09-13: cirrove and cirrove-desktop 0.1.0~dev.r351.ge9a91a4 upgraded in place to r370.g46de988 with apt in the Ubuntu VM, over a signed-in account. After the upgrade the account came back ready and mounted, the keyring grant was still readable, and the index still held all 184,053 items -- so nothing reindexed and no credential was lost across a real package upgrade. STILL NOT DONE: the same run with uploads pending at the moment of the upgrade, and the rollback -- install version N over N-1 on a machine with pending uploads, confirm they finish, roll back to N-1 and confirm it refuses cleanly rather than half-works; the settings file's version guard is held by accounts::tests::a_settings_file_from_a_newer_version_is_refused_rather_than_read. UPDATE 2026-09-14: measured with a live account rather than reasoned about, r409 to r418 and back on Fedora. Settings and credentials survive both directions -- the account still mounted with all 184053 items, the credential id byte-for-byte unchanged, the pin still resident, exactly one Files extension, and no sign-in asked for at any point. One defect found and fixed: the upgrade replaces the files and leaves the daemon and tray running from deleted binaries, so the person stays on the version they just replaced with nothing saying so; the daemon now reports restart_required and the window says it. The schema guard this row rests on was NOT exercised: r409 and r418 write the same format, so the rollback never met a newer state and nothing had to be refused. STILL NOT DONE: pending work, the third noun in the row -- the Fedora account is read-only, so nothing was queued to protect. That needs a write-consented account. See docs/benchmarks/upgrade-and-rollback.json. TICKED 2026-09-14. The third noun is now measured. On the Ubuntu VM with write consent, three files were written with the provider unreachable -- blocked at tcp/443 from inside, because pulling the virtual cable cuts ssh with it -- and queued as pending. apt-get install replaced both packages with all six journal entries naming them still present, the daemon was then restarted onto the new binary while they were still queued and they were still there, and 52 seconds after the provider returned all three finished with nobody retrying them. They were read back through the Fedora VM's mount of the same drive with their exact contents: a file the uploading daemon calls done is not evidence, a file another machine can read is. stuck_changes stayed 0 throughout -- waiting for a provider is pending, not stuck, and calling it stuck would send someone to discard work that was about to succeed. Files removed to the recycle bin afterwards. Settings and credentials were covered in the first run the same day.
rows.asserted_by: clean_handoff::schema_seven_migration_preserves_pending_work_and_refuses_future_schema, unlinked_files::schema_eight_migration_keeps_pending_streams_and_newer_schema_is_refused, local_directories::schema_thirteen_migrates_and_missing_or_future_destination_state_fails_closed, namespace_objects::schema_six_working_files_keep_confirmed_remote_bindings_and_pending_bytes, and the store's own tests of user_version handling; accounts.rs holds the running-daemon refusal. accounts::tests::a_settings_file_from_a_newer_version_is_refused_rather_than_read for the settings file. The rollback half rests on the schema guards the store and the journal already carry and their unit tests; the measured rollback did not exercise them, because r409 and r370 write the same format, and that is recorded as unproven rather than passed.

rows.text: Clean uninstall and explicit retention/removal choices for local data. Measured on a machine with a live account and 2.6 GB of state ([the record](benchmarks/clean-uninstall.json)): nothing packaged survives, the person's data and their keyring grant are left alone, and the mount unmounts cleanly when the session ends. The choice is now the program's rather than the documentation's -- `cirrove local-data` reports what is kept and `--discard-removed` reclaims what an earlier removal set aside, which nothing had ever listed again.
rows.evidence: TICKED 2026-09-14 on a Fedora 44 VM with the owner's account mounted, one file pinned, a credential in an unlocked keyring and 2.6 GB of state; the packages were removed with all of it running, which is the honest case because nobody unmounts first. Clean: a find over /usr and /etc for anything named cirrove returned nothing, the state directory was untouched, the keyring grant survived labelled 'Cirrove Microsoft account' so a person can find it, and stopping the service -- what logging out does -- unmounted cleanly with no stale handle. One oddity recorded rather than fixed: the removal leaves the daemon running from a deleted binary still serving the mount until the session ends, which is untidy but not dangerous, and the window's new restart banner is the nearest thing that speaks to it. The retention/removal choice was the real gap and is now closed: `cirrove forget` has always set a removed connection's data aside instead of deleting it, and nothing ever listed it again, so an uninstall left gigabytes the person believed they had removed. `cirrove local-data` reports each connection, anything set aside, and the total; `--discard-removed` deletes only the set-aside part and says how much it freed.
rows.asserted_by: cirrove-service tests/accounts_local_data.rs: set-aside data is reported with its size and the timestamp parsed from its directory name and counts as the reclaimable total while a live account's does not; discard_set_aside removes it and leaves a live account's cache file present, which is the safety property the whole feature turns on; and an empty removed/ deletes nothing and does not fail. The dangerous version of this command is one that could be talked into deleting a drive still in use, and it is not reachable from any argument.

rows.text: Build and install the daemon and CLI without GTK4/libadwaita present, with separate desktop packaging. The root's default members now exclude the desktop; explicit `--workspace` builds and full contributor checks still include it. A package installation on a clean headless host remains required; headless buildability does not imply unattended browser/keyring setup.
rows.evidence: DONE 2026-09-13. Headless buildability was already checked: the mounted-read-workloads CI job installs neither libgtk-4-dev nor libadwaita-1-dev, asserts their absence, builds the daemon and CLI in release and runs the CLI. What was missing was the other half -- a package installation on a host that has no desktop -- because the deb and rpm jobs install onto runners where the desktop libraries were installed minutes earlier to build the desktop package, so they could say the Depends field names no desktop library but not that the daemon runs without one. The headless-package-install job now installs the core package alone into a clean ubuntu:24.04 container: it fails first if the container already has libgtk-4 or libadwaita, so the test cannot pass vacuously; installs with --no-install-recommends, because the package recommends gnome-keyring and xdg-utils and pulling them in would test apt's defaults rather than what the daemon requires; asserts afterwards that nothing GTK arrived and that neither binary names one in NEEDED; runs both; then installs the desktop package in the same container and asserts the opposite, that GTK does arrive and cirrove-desktop links it -- so the split is shown in both directions rather than only the direction that is easy to pass; and finally purges and checks nothing survives. Every step green on CI run 34762849239 (2026-09-13). Separate desktop packaging is the cirrove/cirrove-desktop split those jobs install.
rows.asserted_by: CI job headless-package-install for the packaged install on a desktop-free host, and mounted-read-workloads for the build; the root's default members exclude the desktop crate, held by the workspace manifest.

rows.text: Tagged release and verified installation from the published artifacts.
rows.evidence: NOT DONE 2026-09-13, but no longer undefined: docs/release-procedure.md says what a release is -- the blockers closed, CI green, versions agreeing across Cargo.toml and the three packaging sources, a tag, the PKGBUILD checksum from the tag, packages from a clean chroot and from the tag's CI artefacts, SHA256SUMS signed, installation on a clean machine per family through a reboot, a second build compared for reproducibility, a GitHub release. docs/changelog.md holds the Unreleased entry. What blocks the first tag is listed in docs/distribution.md. NOT DONE: every step of it, and the release key decision. 2026-09-17: the release key decision is now a choice between four written options rather than an open question -- docs/release-procedure.md, section 'The signature, and the one decision it needs'. A: GitHub artifact attestations, no key to hold, verified with `gh attestation verify`, needs two CI permissions it does not have and covers only artifacts CI built. B: an OpenPGP release key, offline-verifiable with the gpg on every machine, at the cost of a private key one person keeps for the life of the project; there is none on this machine today. C: both. D: unsigned and said so. The recommendation is A for 0.1.0, because the failure mode of B is a lost or leaked key held by one person and there is no signed channel yet whose metadata would need one -- signed APT and COPR are a separate row that explicitly does not gate this release. It is the owner's call and nothing was generated or changed in CI on its behalf. Everything else on this row waits on the milestone-1 rows, whose measurements are running: the capped-memory window in the Ubuntu VM closes 2026-09-17 18:35 and the twenty-four hour G7 run in the Fedora VM closes 2026-09-18 06:45. DECIDED AND BUILT 2026-09-17: the account owner chose A, GitHub artifact attestations. All three package jobs in ci.yml now attest what they build with actions/attest-build-provenance pinned to v4.2.2, each carrying id-token: write and attestations: write of its own (naming any permission at a job replaces the workflow's whole set, so contents: read is repeated beside them). The attestation is made BEFORE the upload, so a release publishes the file the workflow signed rather than one that passed through something afterwards, and it runs on every push and pull request rather than only at a release -- a mechanism exercised once a year is one that is broken when it is needed. A stranger verifies with `gh attestation verify <file> --repo Dandiccf/cirrove` and needs no key. Two consequences are written into the procedure: SHA256SUMS ships unsigned with each package carrying its own attestation and the release body saying so, and step 8's published Arch package now comes from the tagged commit's arch-packages artefact rather than a local clean chroot, because an attestation covers what CI built and nothing else; the local build remains step 12's reproducibility comparison. No private key exists and none is needed. PROVEN the same day, not assumed: CI run 35185096527 attested the three Arch packages, and the artefact was downloaded again and verified from a directory unrelated to the build -- repository Dandiccf/cirrove, commit a9e47dbf, workflow .github/workflows/ci.yml, subject cirrove-0.1.0dev.r522.ga9e47db-1-x86_64.pkg.tar.zst, exit 0. `gh attestation verify` prints nothing on success, which is recorded because an empty output reads like a failure. CLOSED 2026-09-18. v0.1.0 is tagged at 1543bab, CI is green on it, and the release is published with the seven packages, SHA256SUMS and the changelog entry as its body. Verified FROM THE PUBLISHED ARTEFACTS rather than from what was uploaded: downloaded again with `gh release download`, `sha256sum -c SHA256SUMS` clean on all seven, all seven attestations verified naming commit 1543bab, and a clean-machine install of those exact files on Arch through a reboot and a removal. Reproducibility is recorded as NOT achieved with what differed -- same compiler, every data file identical, the four binaries embedding the path they were built in -- rather than skipped or claimed; docs/validation.md carries it, and what would close it. Signing is option A from this row's own decision: no key exists, each package is attested by the workflow that built it, and SHA256SUMS ships unsigned and says so, because it is a convenience for checking a download arrived intact and the attestation is the evidence.
